task: Add a dedicated 'sandbox tab' to the chrome-bridge MCP so every page action targets one auto-created, reused dedicated tab by tabId (not the active tab) and keeps working while the tab is backgrounded — with captureTab of that background tab done via a chrome.debugger/CDP Page.captureScreenshot session, the first deliberate slice of the project's long-OPEN CDP-vs-DOM fork.

analysis.objective: Add an auto-created, reused 'sandbox tab' to the chrome-bridge MCP so every page action targets that one dedicated tab by tabId and keeps working while the tab is backgrounded — with captureTab of that background tab done via a chrome.debugger/CDP Page.captureScreenshot session, the first deliberate slice of the project's long-OPEN CDP-vs-DOM fork.
analysis.successDefinition: Measurable 'done and correct' bar (each is checkable): (1) The extension lazily creates ONE dedicated sandbox tab on first need and reuses the same tab across subsequent commands; its tabId is persisted in chrome.storage.local so it survives a service-worker suspension, and a missing/stale tabId is validated (chrome.tabs.get) and transparently recreated before the next act. (2) Every existing page action (getPageText, readPage, findElement, clickElement, typeText, executeScript, clickAt, hover, navigateTo/Back/Forward, reloadTab, readConsoleMessages, readNetworkRequests) now resolves its target to the sandbox tab's tabId instead of queryActiveTab() — proved by unit tests asserting the handlers pass the sandbox tabId (no queryActiveTab in the resolve path) and by a live Chrome check driving the sandbox tab while a DIFFERENT tab is focused. (3) captureTab on the sandbox tab returns a real PNG of the background tab via chrome.debugger + Page.captureScreenshot, verified in live Chrome by screenshotting the sandbox tab while another tab is focused/active and confirming the image shows the sandbox tab's content, not the focused tab's. (4) The CDP-vs-DOM fork decision is made and recorded explicitly: option (a) — CDP introduced ONLY for the captureTab background-tab gap, everything else stays DOM (chrome.scripting.executeScript function-injection); option (b) — broader CDP pivot — is explicitly NOT chosen and is flagged as the deferred alternative. (5) tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, and the package's vitest suite all pass; the manifest gains the 'debugger' permission without breaking the existing suite; boky's extension/bridge/verify pipeline is unchanged. (6) The horizon closes only after the live Chrome check runs (per the project rule that a horizon changing the extension ends 'blocked / MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING'), proving the sandbox tab is drivable and screenshottable while unfocused.
assumptions: The sandbox tab is the DEFAULT target of every page action, replacing queryActiveTab() resolution; the active-tab path is not retained as a per-call option this horizon — grounded in the user decision that 'the human never picks it or switches to it,' so a selectable active-tab alternative is deferred.

chrome.scripting.executeScript, chrome.tabs.update/goBack/goForward/reload already accept a tabId and operate on a non-focused tab, so only the target-resolution step and the screenshot path need to change for the DOM actions (confirmed in ports.ts: all five take tabId).

The manifest-declared content scripts (page-script.js, capture-forwarder.js, <all_urls> top-frame) auto-inject on the sandbox tab once it navigates to a real <all_urls> site, so readConsoleMessages / readNetworkRequests already populate per-tab rings for the sandbox tabId with no injection wiring change.

CDP is usable from an MV3 service worker and can attach to a background tab with the 'debugger' permission + <all_urls> host permission; Chrome's 'is being debugged' infobar appears while attached and is accepted as a visible side effect.

Page.captureScreenshot returns the sandbox tab's current rendered viewport regardless of focus, because a backgrounded tab still keeps its layout rendered (static paint), even though animations are throttled while hidden.
The tabId-targeting blocker in blockers.md is resolved by the user's decision toward a single dedicated sandbox tab; this supersedes the next-horizon brief's recommendation to keep gap #5 deferred.
A sandbox tab that is still about:blank / a fresh new-tab has no captured entries and returns empty-but-valid capture reads, matching the existing empty-read behavior for an unseen tab.
risks: chrome.debugger.attach to a background tab may be blocked or fail from an MV3 service worker ('Cannot attach to this target', permission not honored outside an interactive gesture, or the tab discarded by memory pressure); if attach fails, captureTab cannot be satisfied by the minimal option-(a) CDP — this is exactly the CDP-vs-DOM fork tension. Mitigation: a live-Chrome probe is the first task; if a background tab cannot be debugger-attached, option (a) is falsified and must be escalated, not patched.

Option (a)'s 'everything else stays DOM' assumption may not survive contact with CDP: Page.captureScreenshot sits naturally beside Runtime.evaluate and Input.dispatch*, so the minimal CDP island can silently sprawl into trusted input / scroll / keyboard. This scope-creep is a real process risk, not hypothetical — guard by explicitly tracking every CDP surface added.

Re-pointing the default target to a sandbox tab changes observable behavior for any existing caller/recorded verification that assumed 'drives the active tab,' and because the sandbox tab stays unfocused the human no longer sees what the agent is doing; a mis-target (e.g. acting on a stale tabId after browser restart re-uses an id) is only visible to the agent. Every act must validate the tabId and recreate when missing.

MV3 service-worker suspension: the sandbox tabId must persist in chrome.storage.local, and the create-if-missing path must be idempotent and race-safe — two commands arriving near a wake could both create a tab. tabs.create is a new async chrome port that must be added and tested.

CDP session lifecycle leaks: attach → Page.captureScreenshot → detach per screenshot is simplest, but a detach failure or a suspension mid-session leaves a dangling debugger target; the lifecycle must handle errors (listen to chrome.debugger.onDetach) and not leak attachments across screenshots.

SECURITY/attack-surface note (no caller acceptance criteria supplied, so flagged as a judgment call rather than a conflict): adding the 'debugger' permission is a powerful, privileged grant letting the extension read/modify any page and act outside user intent; it is necessary and deliberate for background-tab capture, but the broadened surface should be visible to a reviewer, not incidental.

A reader may assume 'we added CDP, so executeScript now works on strict-CSP sites (github.com / reddit.com)' — option (a) does NOT deliver CSP-ignoring Runtime.evaluate, so that previously-documented hard failure stays. This is a scoping landmine; the decision record must state it plainly.
Multiple tool-callers use the MCP image block; the CDP capture must be mapped back to the same base64-image content block (dataUrl prefix stripped) or the existing captureTab rendering breaks.
outOfScope: Broad CDP pivot beyond the screenshot gap (Runtime.evaluate to replace executeScript, Input.dispatchKeyEvent / drag for trusted input, page scrolling, full-page scroll-capture, file upload): option (a) keeps the stack DOM except Page.captureScreenshot — the rest is the deferred CDP-vs-DOM expansion the brief warns against pulling in early.

General tab management (a listTabs tool, tabs_create/close/switch, multi-tab, cross-window): the horizon commits to exactly ONE dedicated sandbox tab; opening/closing/selecting arbitrary tabs is a separate gap.

Keyboard action (gap #3) and Scroll action (gap #4): the brief's alternative recommended slices, not taken here — DOM feasibility of synthetic key events / scroll-then-click is never measured this horizon.
Full-page and element-clipped screenshots plus format/quality options: captureTab stays a viewport PNG; the CDP step only makes it background-capable, not full-page.
The result-size-cap location/threshold decision (extension-side per-action vs generic MCP-layer vs none): still OPEN and deliberately deferred; CDP screenshots do not change the cap question.
iframe / all_frames capture: content scripts stay top-frame only; background-tab targeting does not extend to subframes.
Window/viewport resize, image injection, batch actions, cookie/storage inspection, JS dialog handling: the medium/lower-impact gap list — not touched by tab targeting.

Preserving the active-tab path as a selectable per-call option: the sandbox tab replaces the default target; a retained 'active tab' alternative is deferred under the user's 'human never picks or switches' decision.
Boky's extension / BridgeRelayModule / extension-mcp.mjs: unchanged everywhere — chrome-bridge is standalone and boky is never migrated into it.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The task is browser-driver machinery — MV3 extension target-resolution plus a CDP/screenshot adapter for an MCP tool — with no business entities or rules a domain expert would recognize, matching the project's recorded vision classification.

discoveryFindings.finding: ChromePorts exposes exactly seven methods: queryActiveTab() -> ActiveTab|undefined (ActiveTab = {id, windowId}); executeScript(tabId, func, args, options?); updateTab(tabId, {url}); goBack(tabId); goForward(tabId); reload(tabId); captureVisibleTab(windowId) -> data:image/png URL. Six of seven take a tabId already; captureVisibleTab is the exception and takes windowId, NOT tabId.
discoveryFindings.implication: Re-pointing the six DOM/nav actions to the sandbox tab is a pure resolution change (they already accept tabId). But captureTab cannot be re-targeted by passing a tabId to captureVisibleTab — it is window-scoped, so the chrome.debugger/CDP Page.captureScreenshot path is mandatory, not optional. New chrome surfaces (tabs.get, tabs.create, chrome.storage.local, chrome.debugger.attach/sendCommand/detach) do not exist in ChromePorts and must be added in a sibling interface.

discoveryFindings.finding: All 14 non-ping handlers resolve the target identically via `const tab = await ports.queryActiveTab()` then `if (tab === undefined) return NO_ACTIVE_TAB`. No action's params carry a tabId anywhere.
discoveryFindings.implication: This is one mechanical substitution, not 14 bespoke edits: replace the queryActiveTab call with a sandbox-tab resolver. The NO_ACTIVE_TAB sentinel's wording becomes semantically wrong and should be renamed.

discoveryFindings.finding: captureTab currently does queryActiveTab() then `ports.captureVisibleTab(tab.windowId)` and returns {result:{dataUrl}}. PageActionResults.captureTab = {dataUrl: string}. The MCP server special-cases captureTab -> imageResult(stripDataUrlPrefix(...)).
discoveryFindings.implication: The CDP Page.captureScreenshot response is {data: base64} with NO dataUrl prefix. To keep the existing MCP rendering and the {dataUrl} protocol type unchanged, the CDP handler should re-emit {dataUrl: 'data:image/png;base64,<b64>'}. Needs a new port method wrapping attach -> captureScreenshot -> detach, plus onDetach handling.

discoveryFindings.area: Protocol contract for adding a param vs a new action
discoveryFindings.finding: PAGE_ACTIONS is a 16-entry as-const tuple. Adding a NEW action requires 6-place edits; adding a PARAM touches only 3.
discoveryFindings.implication: This task needs NEITHER a new action NOR a per-call param — the sandbox tab is the default target. protocol/actions.ts, PageActionParams/Results, the MCP catalog, and the hardcoded-16 parity tests are all untouched.

discoveryFindings.area: Service-worker wiring / absence of create-tab surface
discoveryFindings.finding: startServiceWorker(deps:{alarms, ports, capturePorts, socketFactory, url?}) wires keepalive + captureStore + dispatcher + bridge client; there is NO chrome.tabs.create/get call and NO chrome.storage.* usage in src. tabs.onRemoved handled in capture-ports.ts -> installCaptureIntake -> store.evict(tabId).
discoveryFindings.implication: Sandbox-tab create/validate/persist is greenfield. The resolver should be a new injected dependency (sibling to CapturePorts, e.g. SandboxTabPorts/DebuggerPorts) rather than widening ChromePorts. Capture rings are evicted via the existing onTabRemoved path.

discoveryFindings.finding: Both read handlers resolve the active tab then call captureStore.readConsole(tab.id)/readNetwork(tab.id). The store keys rings by tabId; intake keys by sender.tab.id; eviction is tabs.onRemoved. Content scripts are manifest-declared at <all_urls>, document_start, top-frame.
discoveryFindings.implication: The sandbox tab populates its own per-tab rings with NO injection-wiring change once it navigates to a real site. Only target resolution changes. Do not touch capture-store/forwarder/ports.

discoveryFindings.finding: permissions are [tabs, activeTab, scripting, storage, alarms], host_permissions [<all_urls>], NO 'debugger'. 'storage' already present.
discoveryFindings.implication: 'debugger' is a one-line addition to the permissions array. chrome.storage.local persistence needs no manifest change. High-privilege grant — surface to reviewers.

discoveryFindings.finding: grep for debugger / Page.captureScreenshot / Runtime.evaluate / Input.dispatch / chrome.debugger returns zero code hits; only prose in the inventory markdown.
discoveryFindings.filePath: tools/chrome-bridge/full inventory and gap analysis against the claude-in-chrome MCP.md
discoveryFindings.implication: The debugger surface is greenfield. A fresh port module (chromeDebuggerPorts) with attach/sendCommand/detach + onDetach listener must be written and unit-tested from scratch.

discoveryFindings.area: Tests that a tabId/debugger change must not break
discoveryFindings.finding: page-actions.unit.test.ts and service-worker.unit.test.ts each define a full fakePorts() implementing all 7 ChromePorts methods; page-actions tests assert vi.mocked(ports.queryActiveTab) toHaveBeenCalled() and executeScript toHaveBeenCalledWith(7,...) in ~10 places, plus several 'no active tab' tests. capture-ports.unit.test.ts uses vi.stubGlobal('chrome', stub).
discoveryFindings.implication: Adding any method to ChromePorts breaks BOTH fakePorts objects at typecheck. Re-pointing resolution breaks the queryActiveTab assertions and 'no active tab' tests — exactly the assertions the success criterion wants rewritten. A new chrome.debugger port impl needs its own stubGlobal('chrome', {debugger:...}).

discoveryFindings.area: Test placement / vitest / lint hook false-positives
discoveryFindings.finding: vitest includes unit+int tests, environment 'node', no jsdom. Package verify = tsc --noEmit + eslint . --max-warnings 0 + vitest run. Repo-root PostToolUse hook runs ROOT eslint on chrome-bridge files and can false-positive.
discoveryFindings.implication: New tests must be pure Node (vi.stubGlobal for browser globals). Expect possible hook false-positives; resolve within the package eslint config. The live-Chrome check remains manual.

discoveryFindings.finding: Root .testguard.json ignore list includes '/ports\.ts$' and '/types\.ts$' (exact anchored), with requireSymbolMentions:true.
discoveryFindings.implication: ports.ts and types.ts are exempt, but a NEW file such as sandbox-ports.ts or debugger-ports.ts does NOT match '/ports\.ts$' and must ship a co-located unit test covering each exported symbol.

phases.name: Verify Chrome can screenshot a background tab
phases.goal: Prove in a real Chrome session that chrome.debugger can attach to a NON-focused tab from the extension service worker and that Page.captureScreenshot returns a PNG of that background tab, before any CDP port code is built on that assumption. This is the de-risking gate the whole background-tab screenshot feature depends on.
phases.rationale: The feature screenshots the dedicated sandbox tab while it sits unfocused in the background. Chrome's own chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab can only capture the focused tab, so the plan uses chrome.debugger + CDP Page.captureScreenshot, which targets a tab by id. But it is not established that an MV3 service worker can attach to a non-active tab: MV3 service workers can be suspended, a background tab may be discarded under memory pressure, and Chrome may reject attaching to a target the user does not have in focus. If attach fails, the whole feature — and the requirement that background-tab screenshots work — is not buildable as scoped, so this must be validated first as a hard gate.
filesAffected: tools/chrome-bridge/extension/manifest.json (add the 'debugger' permission, which the probe needs to attach)
tools/chrome-bridge/ (a throwaway real-Chrome probe; no committed product code beyond the manifest permission)
changes: Add 'debugger' to the permissions array in manifest.json (the <all_urls> host permission is already present, the other requirement for chrome.debugger.attach).

Run a real Chrome check: open one tab in the foreground and a second tab in the background, then from the extension's service worker call chrome.debugger.attach({tabId: <backgroundTab>}, '1.3') and chrome.debugger.sendCommand({tabId}, 'Page.captureScreenshot', {format:'png'}).
Confirm the returned image is a PNG of the BACKGROUND tab, not the focused tab; record the verdict.
If attach fails or returns the focused tab, STOP and raise it — the CDP approach is falsified and the horizon needs a replan; do not patch around it.
On pass, remove the throwaway probe; the durable CDP port is built in the later phase. The 'debugger' permission lands here.
phases.expectedResult: A recorded real-Chrome verdict that chrome.debugger can attach to a background tab from the service worker and that Page.captureScreenshot returns that background tab's PNG, with the 'debugger' permission added to the manifest to enable it. If the verdict is negative, the phase ends blocked with the proof that the CDP screenshot design is not buildable as scoped.

rubric.label: 'debugger' permission added, nothing else changed
rubric.ruleStatement: The chrome-bridge extension manifest must declare the 'debugger' permission that chrome.debugger.attach requires, and the manifest delta must be exactly that one permission. Without it the probe fails with a permission error and produces a false-negative verdict. Scale: 10 = 'debugger' present, diff vs previous commit contains no other permission change, throwaway probe outside build/ship path; 8 = 'debugger' present with a small justified extra; minScore 7.
passCriteria: Open manifest.json and confirm 'debugger' appears in the permissions array.
Diff the manifest against the previous commit: 'debugger' is the only permission addition, no existing permission or host pattern was removed or narrowed.
Confirm the throwaway probe is not committed under a directory the extension builds/ships.
failureExamples: The probe never adds 'debugger' — attach rejects with a permission error and a false negative is recorded.
The dev adds 'debugger' but also narrows the host permission, changing runtime capability beyond the intended one-permission delta.
The throwaway probe is committed under an extension build path and stays after the gate passes.

rubric.label: Attach succeeds on a non-focused tab, by explicit tabId
rubric.ruleStatement: chrome.debugger.attach must be called with the intended non-focused tab's tabId and resolve cleanly, and the verdict must establish this attached tab is NOT the focused one. Scale: 10 = attach resolves on an explicitly-recorded non-focused tabId AND an independent corroborating signal shows it cannot be the focused tab; 8 = attach succeeds on the recorded background tabId with the focused tab's id recorded as different; minScore 7.
passCriteria: The probe records the id of BOTH the focused tab (chrome.tabs.query({active:true})) and the background tab, and the verdict shows the two ids are different.
chrome.debugger.attach({tabId: <backgroundTabId>}, '1.3') resolves without error.
The verdict states the attached tabId is the non-focused one and shows an independent signal it was not the active tab.
If attach rejects, the verdict quotes the exact error and closes the phase as BLOCKED.
failureExamples: The dev grabs a tab id from a query that returns the focused tab, attaches to it, and records a pass — the background tab was never the target.
A 'background' boolean is set in bookkeeping but the tab is never kept unfocused.
A first run left the debugger attached; a second attach fails and the dev treats the first run's success as the gate passing.

rubric.label: The captured PNG is the background tab, not the focused tab
rubric.ruleStatement: Page.captureScreenshot over the attached debugger must return a valid PNG whose content verifiably matches the BACKGROUND tab, and evidence must rule out captureVisibleTab or a tab brought to focus. Scale: 10 = capture decodes to a real PNG, content matches a unique marker only on the background tab, a focused-tab negative control differs, and path is proven Page.captureScreenshot over the debugger; 8 = unique-marker match and CDP path confirmed and tab stated unfocused, no focused-tab negative control; minScore 7.
passCriteria: Before capturing, the background tab is given unique content (unique title and large unique banner text, or unique hostname).
The captured bytes decode to a real PNG (correct signature, non-trivial size, not single-color).
The verdict shows the captured image contains the background tab's unique marker and states it matches the background tab.
The verdict records the API path: chrome.debugger.sendCommand({tabId}, 'Page.captureScreenshot') NOT captureVisibleTab, and the tab stayed unfocused.
failureExamples: Both tabs point at the same URL so 'a PNG returned' is recorded as success with no way to distinguish the background tab.
After CDP capture failed, the dev silently added a captureVisibleTab fallback or focused the tab, and recorded a pass.

rubric.label: Attach runs from the MV3 service worker and repeats cleanly
rubric.ruleStatement: The attach/capture must be exercised from the extension service worker — the context the durable CDP port will run in, where MV3 suspension can kill an in-flight session — and must detach cleanly so a second attempt succeeds. Scale: 10 = two consecutive attach-capture-detach cycles from the service worker in one browser session both succeed with detach recorded; 9 = single cycle from the service worker with clean detach, note second run not performed; minScore 6.
passCriteria: The verdict states the attach/capture code ran in the extension service worker context, not a popup/content script/devtools console.
The probe completes with chrome.debugger.detach({tabId}), and the verdict records the detach.
The probe runs a second full cycle and the second attach resolves cleanly.
failureExamples: The probe is run from a devtools console or dashboard page so attach works but the durable port runs in the SW where suspension can kill it.
The cycle runs once, captures fine, never detaches, and is never re-run; a manual second attempt fails with 'Another debugger is already attached'.

rubric.label: A negative result is recorded as BLOCKED, not worked around
rubric.ruleStatement: The recorded verdict must be a faithful record: a genuine pass counts only when the background-tab proof is real; a genuine failure is recorded as BLOCKED, not disguised behind a worked-around pass. Scale: 10 = genuine failure quotes the error, states BLOCKED, leaves no worked-around pass, and the throwaway probe is removed; 8 = genuine failure recorded accurately; minScore 7.
passCriteria: The verdict is recorded in something durable that survives the tab closing.
There is no worked-around branch that produces 'a screenshot' without attaching to a non-focused background tab.
If attach/capture fails, the verdict quotes the exact error and ends the phase as BLOCKED.
A recorded pass only stands if the background-tab proof is actually present in the recorded evidence.
failureExamples: The dev hits an attach error then gets 'working' output by focusing the tab or using captureVisibleTab and records a pass.
The verdict exists only as a terminal screenshot/live console capture that is gone by review time.

phases.healerHint: The gate fails most often because both tabs point at the same URL so 'a PNG returned' is recorded as a pass without any way to prove it is the background tab — the fastest fix is to give the background tab an unmistakable identity (unique title plus a large unique banner) and also capture the focused tab to show the two images differ.

phases.name: Add sandbox tab port module
phases.goal: Introduce a new port (a typed interface over a slice of the Chrome extension API) that guarantees exactly one dedicated sandbox tab exists and returns its numeric tabId, so later phases can make every page action target that tab instead of whatever is focused.
phases.rationale: Today every page action acts on the browser's active (focused) tab. When a tool drives a tab in the background, a human clicking around the browser steals the target mid-command. This phase adds the machinery to own a single dedicated background tab: create it once, remember its id, reuse it. The chrome tab APIs it needs (chrome.tabs.create, chrome.tabs.get, chrome.storage.local) do not exist anywhere in the codebase yet, so a brand-new port module is required.
changes: Create the SandboxTabPorts interface with one method resolveTabId(): Promise<number> that returns the id of the one dedicated sandbox tab, creating or recreating it when needed.

Implement chromeSandboxTabPorts(): read the persisted sandbox tab id from chrome.storage.local; validate it still exists via chrome.tabs.get; if the id is missing or stale (get rejects or returns undefined), create a new background tab with chrome.tabs.create({ active: false }) and write the new id back to chrome.storage.local.
Make the create path re-entrant (validate before create, persist promptly) so two near-simultaneous commands don't both spawn a tab.

Write sandbox-ports.unit.test.ts stubbing the chrome global with vi.stubGlobal — covering: returns a stored valid id, creates + persists when nothing is stored, recreates when the stored id is stale, and persists the created id.
inputs: chrome.storage.local (the storage permission is already declared in the manifest)
phases.expectedResult: A new sandbox-ports.ts exporting the SandboxTabPorts interface and the chromeSandboxTabPorts() implementation, covered by sandbox-ports.unit.test.ts for every exported symbol (the resolveTabId create / validate / recreate / persist paths). No other file in the package is touched by this phase.

rubric.label: One dedicated tab, reused across calls
rubric.ruleStatement: Calling resolveTabId repeatedly while the stored tab is alive must return the same numeric tabId every time and must never create a new tab. Scale: 10 = id is stable forever (every call reuses the stored id, zero chrome.tabs.create, resolved value always a positive integer); 8 = reuses the stored id correctly; minScore 7.
passCriteria: Call resolveTabId twice with a stored live id; assert both returned values are strictly equal.
Assert the returned value is a number: typeof number, Number.isInteger, and > 0.
Assert chrome.tabs.create was never invoked on the reuse path (spy call count 0).
Assert the returned id is exactly the id passed to chrome.tabs.get for validation.
failureExamples: The persisted id comes through async get as an object or string, so the reuse path returns non-number and silently falls through to create.
The dev writes the created id under a different key than the one read, so reuse reads nothing and spawns a new tab every call.

rubric.label: Create on empty storage, focus-safe and persisted
rubric.ruleStatement: When no id is stored, resolveTabId must create exactly one tab with active:false (so the sandbox tab never steals focus) and write the created id back to chrome.storage.local before the promise resolves. Scale: 10 = creation, focus-safety, and persistence all evidenced and correctly ordered; 8 = correct create+persist that may persist after the caller has the id; minScore 7.
passCriteria: With empty storage, resolveTabId calls chrome.tabs.create exactly once with active: false.
After resolveTabId resolves, chrome.storage.local holds the created id so a subsequent call reuses it.
The persisted tab id is a bare number, not {id:n} or a string.
On the empty-storage path resolveTabId resolves with the new id after the create settles.
failureExamples: The dev passes { active: true } or omits active (defaults to true), so creating the sandbox tab steals focus — and a test that only checks 'a tab id was returned' still passes.
The dev persists {id: newTab.id} or under the wrong key, breaking the round-trip reuse.

rubric.label: Recreate when the stored id is dead
rubric.ruleStatement: When the persisted id no longer names a live tab (get rejects, or resolves to an undefined/closed tab), resolveTabId must create a replacement background tab and persist its id. Scale: 10 = every stale signal handled and no dead id left in storage; 8 = correct recreation for the common get-rejects case; minScore 6.
passCriteria: Prime storage with an id whose chrome.tabs.get rejects; call resolveTabId; assert it creates once and returns the new id, and storage holds the new id.
Handle the stale case where get resolves but the returned tab is not a real live tab (e.g. returned tab.id !== stored id, or tab is undefined).
Assert the replacement tab was created with active: false.
failureExamples: The dev detects staleness only via try/catch around get, omitting the case where get resolves to an undefined/closed tab — a dead id that resolves is returned.
In the stale branch the dev creates the replacement but forgets to persist it, so every call re-enters stale and leaks a new tab.

rubric.label: Re-entrant: no double spawn under overlap
rubric.ruleStatement: Two overlapping resolveTabId calls must not both spawn a tab: once a create is in flight, a concurrent caller observes the same in-flight result rather than issuing a second chrome.tabs.create. Scale: 10 = a concurrency test proves exactly one chrome.tabs.create under interleaved non-awaited calls; 8 = shares the create work but may not be provably race-free; minScore 7.
passCriteria: The test has a concurrency case: stub chrome.tabs.create to stay pending until released; call resolveTabId twice without awaiting the first; resolve; assert chrome.tabs.create called exactly once and both promises resolve to the same id.
The implementation validates before creating and persists promptly, so a call after the id is known never re-creates.
failureExamples: The dev's 're-entrancy' fix is merely re-reading storage in the create branch with no shared in-flight promise, so two truly concurrent calls both spawn — and a sequential-only suite ships green.
The dev returns a cached id but the cache resets per call or the storage write is not awaited before a subsequent read, so the second overlapping call reads before the write lands.

rubric.label: Unit tests stub chrome and cover every lifecycle path
rubric.ruleStatement: sandbox-ports.unit.test.ts must stub the chrome global with vi.stubGlobal and contain a dedicated test for each lifecycle path (reuse, fresh create, stale recreate), asserting chrome side-effects, and every exported symbol must be exercised. Scale: 10 = each named path has a test AND the stub asserts the exact chrome calls; 8 = each path has a test but the stub only checks the return value; minScore 7.
passCriteria: The test file uses vi.stubGlobal('chrome', ...) and cleanup in afterEach, not a real/partial chrome global.
There are distinct named tests for: stored-valid reuse (no create), empty-storage create+persist, and stale-recreate+persist.
At least one test asserts a chrome side-effect: chrome.tabs.create called with {active:false}, and chrome.storage.set called with the created id under the key resolveTabId reads.
Every exported symbol is referenced by the suite.
failureExamples: The stored-valid test's chrome.tabs.get also rejects (shared stub rejected across tests), so the valid-reuse path is never actually exercised.
The dev stubs chrome but only asserts the resolved value; chrome.storage.set is never asserted, so a persistence key-mismatch ships green.

phases.healerHint: Most likely miss: a read/write storage key mismatch (read 'sandboxTabId', write 'SANDBOX_TAB_ID') plus no shared in-flight create promise means every call or each overlapping pair spawns a fresh tab — use one constant key and hold a single shared create promise so concurrent resolveTabId calls await the same tab.

phases.name: Add CDP debugger screenshot port
phases.goal: Introduce a port that screenshots an arbitrary background tab via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) using chrome.debugger, so a tab that is not focused can still be captured.
phases.rationale: Chrome's built-in chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab can only capture the focused/active tab of a window. The dedicated sandbox tab is deliberately kept unfocused, so capturing it needs CDP's Page.captureScreenshot, which operates on a specific tab regardless of focus. Using chrome.debugger requires the debugger permission (added in the feasibility gate phase).
changes: Add the CaptureDebuggerPorts interface with captureScreenshot(tabId): Promise<string> returning a data:image/png;base64,<b64> URL.

Implement chromeCaptureDebuggerPorts(): call chrome.debugger.attach({tabId}, '1.3'), chrome.debugger.sendCommand({tabId}, 'Page.captureScreenshot', {format:'png'}), read the {data} base64 from the response, wrap it as data:image/png;base64,<b64>, then chrome.debugger.detach in a finally block.

Register a chrome.debugger.onDetach listener so a mid-session detach (worker suspension, the user closing the debugger) cleans up without leaking an attachment; surface attach failures as thrown errors.
Write debugger-ports.unit.test.ts stubbing chrome.debugger — covering attach→sendCommand(captureScreenshot)→detach ordering, the dataUrl prefixing, the onDetach cleanup, and an attach failure.

Record the CDP-vs-DOM decision in the project decisions note: CDP is introduced ONLY for the captureTab background-tab gap; the broader CDP pivot (Runtime.evaluate, Input dispatch, scroll) is NOT chosen and is deferred. The 'debugger' permission is already present by now.
phases.expectedResult: A new debugger-ports.ts exporting the CaptureDebuggerPorts interface and the chromeCaptureDebuggerPorts() implementation, covered by its co-located debugger-ports.unit.test.ts. The CDP-vs-DOM decision record states CDP is limited to Page.captureScreenshot.
phases.compensation: The debugger permission is a privileged, manifest-declared grant with no other consumer yet. To roll back, delete debugger-ports.ts and its test and remove the debugger permission from manifest.json — no other code calls this port, so there is no downstream breakage to unwind.

rubric.label: Screenshot returns a usable data URL
rubric.ruleStatement: captureScreenshot(tabId) resolves to a string that is exactly one valid data:image/png;base64,<b64> URL built from the CDP `{data}` field. Scale: 10 = URL byte-correct AND the missing-`data` case rejects with a clear error; 8 = URL correct for the normal stub path but a gap remains (substitutes 'undefined' if `data` absent); minScore 8.
passCriteria: Confirm one assertion that the resolved string starts with exactly `data:image/png;base64,` (scheme present once, not twice).
Confirm the test decodes the substring and matches the stub PNG bytes — the base64 payload is passed through unmodified.
In debugger-ports.ts, confirm base64 is read from the response's `data` field, not hardcoded or re-derived.
Search for a repeated prefix concatenation to rule out the double-prefix bug.
failureExamples: The function returns raw `{data}` base64 with no scheme, so every test is green but the port hands a non-renderable string.
The wrapper decodes then re-encodes, or prepends the scheme to a value that already has it, yielding a doubled prefix.
A dev accesses `{data}` that is undefined on some tabs and emits `data:image/png;base64,undefined` instead of rejecting.

rubric.label: Debugger detaches on success and failure
rubric.ruleStatement: Every call path runs chrome.debugger.detach, and that detach does not mask the value/error being returned. Scale: 10 = detach in a `finally` AND a detach that throws is swallowed so the original outcome surfaces; 8 = detach runs on common success and error paths; minScore 8.
passCriteria: Locate the detach call and confirm it is inside a `finally` block, not only the success branch.
Confirm a test injects a rejecting sendCommand mock and still asserts detach was called, and the function rejects with the sendCommand error.
Read the flow: the returned error/result is the capture outcome, not a detach exception.
Confirm the success-path assertion checks detach ran after sendCommand.
failureExamples: detach lives only in the success branch, so a sendCommand rejection leaves the tab attached and the next capture fails with 'Another debugger is already attached'.
detach runs on the error path but if it rejects it overwrites the real sendCommand error.
detach is in finally but the test only asserts toHaveBeenCalled on the success mock, so a non-finally version passes CI.

rubric.label: Repeated captures re-attach cleanly
rubric.ruleStatement: Two sequential captureScreenshot calls (success+success and success+failure) both complete without an 'already attached' error. Scale: 10 = explicit test issues a second call after a FAILED first and asserts it succeeds; 8 = the happy second-call works; minScore 7.
passCriteria: Find a test that calls captureScreenshot twice and asserts the second resolves, with attach invoked again.
Confirm a case where the first capture rejects and a subsequent capture still re-attaches.
Read the detach path to confirm it does not leave the tab attached such that reuse errors.
failureExamples: The reject path skips detach, so the second capture hits 'already attached' and the per-action tab flow can only succeed once.
The test only ever runs a single capture, so a re-attach-after-failure bug never surfaces.
detach is awaited but a previous onDetach already removed the attachment, so detach throws on the second path.

rubric.label: onDetach listener is leak-free and resolves in-flight capture
rubric.ruleStatement: The chrome.debugger.onDetach listener is registered without accumulating per-call listeners and rejects a pending capture when the browser detaches mid-capture rather than leaving it unresolved. Scale: 10 = listener added once and removed on completion AND a mid-capture detach rejects the in-flight promise with a clear error; 8 = listener added/removed correctly and rejects in-flight captures; minScore 7.
passCriteria: Confirm onDetach is registered a single time (not inside the per-capture function body) or removed after the first firing.
Confirm a mid-capture detach rejects/resolves the pending promise rather than leaving it hanging.
Confirm the listener's cleanup cannot throw on a second/no-op detach.
In the test, confirm a mocked onDetach event triggers the same cleanup path.
failureExamples: The handler is added per capture call without removeListener, so a long-lived sandbox tab accumulates one listener per action.
The listener cleans up but never rejects the in-flight capture, so under SW suspension the caller's await hangs forever.
A dev relies on chrome.debugger to clean up, so a mid-capture detach leaves a dangling promise and a stale resolver that resolves the wrong later call.

rubric.label: Decision note bounds CDP to the screenshot gap
rubric.ruleStatement: The project decisions note records that CDP is introduced ONLY to close the background-tab captureVisibleTab gap via Page.captureScreenshot, and explicitly states the broader CDP pivot is NOT chosen and deferred; it also reconciles that captureVisibleTab is still the focused-tab path. Scale: 10 = note names the deferred pivot, names the still-in-scope captureVisibleTab path, and states the permission cost consciously; 8 = names the gap and states the pivot is deferred; minScore 6.
passCriteria: Open the project decisions note and confirm a line that says CDP is used only for the background-tab / captureVisibleTab gap, specifically Page.captureScreenshot.
Confirm an explicit statement that Runtime.evaluate, Input.dispatchMouseEvent, and scroll are NOT adopted and are deferred.
Confirm the note does not conflict with the still-in-use captureVisibleTab-for-focused-tab behavior.
Confirm the note mentions the 'debugger' permission or dependency as the accepted cost.
failureExamples: The note says 'added CDP for screenshots' without stating the broader pivot is deferred, so a later engineer reads it as approval to build Runtime.evaluate/Input dispatch next.
The note records the chosen path but never reconciles that the focused tab still uses captureVisibleTab.
The decision is recorded in a code comment no future reviewer will read.

phases.healerHint: Most likely the port returns the raw {data} base64 without the `data:image/png;base64,` prefix (or the test strips the scheme so it still passes) — add the prefix exactly once and make the test assert the full literal prefix and decode the payload, then re-run the whole unit file since a detach/ordering fix often hides behind a passing happy-path case.

phases.name: Point page actions at the sandbox tab
phases.goal: Change every page-action handler that currently resolves the browser's active tab to instead resolve the one dedicated sandbox tab id, so all page actions reliably operate on the same unfocused tab.
phases.rationale: Now that the sandbox tab port exists, the handlers must use it. Today each handler calls ports.queryActiveTab() and aborts with 'no active tab' if none is focused. Replacing that with the sandbox tab's id means commands stop depending on whatever the human happens to be looking at. This is one mechanical substitution across the handlers, not bespoke per-action logic.
changes: Change pageActionHandlers(ports, captureStore) to also take a SandboxTabPorts (the sandbox tab resolver) parameter.

Replace each `const tab = await ports.queryActiveTab(); if (tab === undefined) return NO_ACTIVE_TAB;` block (13 non-captureTab sites, including the readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests closure) with a single `const tabId = await sandboxTab.resolveTabId();` — a throw from the resolver is caught by the existing guard() wrapper.

Replace the NO_ACTIVE_TAB sentinel with a sandbox-specific sentinel and a distinct 'sandbox tab missing and could not be created' error; update the two no-history messages that say 'the active tab' to say 'the sandbox tab'. Leave the captureTab handler's queryActiveTab/windowId path untouched here (it is re-pointed in the next phase).
Wire chromeSandboxTabPorts() into startServiceWorker and pass it into pageActionHandlers.

Update page-actions.unit.test.ts: drop the queryActiveTab assertions for the re-pointed handlers, add a fake SandboxTabPorts returning a fixed tab id (7), and assert each handler calls resolveTabId then passes the sandbox id into executeScript / updateTab / goBack / goForward / reload / readConsole / readNetwork (proving no queryActiveTab remains in the resolve path). Keep queryActiveTab in fakePorts because captureTab still uses it until the next phase.
Update service-worker.unit.test.ts to supply the new SandboxTabPorts dependency to startServiceWorker.
inputs: the existing page-actions.unit.test.ts and service-worker.unit.test.ts fakes
phases.expectedResult: pageActionHandlers resolves every non-captureTab action to the sandbox tab id via resolveTabId(), with the unit tests proving no queryActiveTab call remains in the resolve path (the old 'no active tab' tests are rewritten to assert the sandbox-resolver failure path).
phases.compensation: To roll back, restore the queryActiveTab resolution blocks and the old NO_ACTIVE_TAB sentinel in each handler, revert the pageActionHandlers signature, and restore the original fake in service-worker.unit.test.ts.

rubric.label: Every non-captureTab handler resolves via resolveTabId with no active-tab call left
rubric.ruleStatement: Every non-captureTab handler resolves its target ONLY through sandboxTab.resolveTabId(); no handler may still resolve the active tab. Scale: 10 = a text search for queryActiveTab matches only the captureTab handler's windowId block, and every other handler begins tab access with await sandboxTab.resolveTabId(); 8 = all re-pointed but one carries a dead unreachable active-tab branch; minScore 8.
passCriteria: Search page-actions.ts for `queryActiveTab`. Every match must sit inside the captureTab handler body.
For each of the 13 non-captureTab handlers, confirm the first tab-access line is `await sandboxTab.resolveTabId()`.
Open the shared readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests closure and confirm it calls resolveTabId and no longer queryActiveTab.
Confirm no handler still short-circuits resolution with an early `if (tab === undefined) return` abort.
failureExamples: The dev re-pointed per-action handlers but the shared readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests closure still calls queryActiveTab, so console/network reads still target the active tab.
The dev added resolveTabId but forgot to delete the old queryActiveTab line in one handler, so it still passes the ACTIVE tab's id.
A handler keeps a now-unreachable old `if (tab === undefined) return NO_ACTIVE_TAB;` branch.

rubric.label: captureTab keeps its active-tab / windowId resolution (deferred to next phase)
rubric.ruleStatement: The captureTab handler must keep resolving via ports.queryActiveTab() and the windowId path exactly as before, and must NOT call sandboxTab.resolveTabId(). Scale: 10 = diffing page-actions.ts against git HEAD shows captureTab's resolution lines byte-for-byte unchanged and captureTab references no resolveTabId; 8 = behavior identical with a cosmetic touch; minScore 8.
passCriteria: Diff page-actions.ts against git baseline: the captureTab handler's queryActiveTab and windowId resolution lines must be unchanged, no resolveTabId added.
Search the captureTab handler body for resolveTabId — it must not appear.
Confirm no comment/TODO claims captureTab was migrated to the sandbox tab.
failureExamples: The dev interpreted the task as 'remove all queryActiveTab' and swapped captureTab over to resolveTabId, breaking the deliberate handoff.
They pulled captureTab into a shared helper and changed its queryActiveTab to resolveTabId for uniformity.

rubric.label: Distinct sandbox sentinel, caught resolver throw, and updated 'sandbox tab' messages
rubric.ruleStatement: When the sandbox tab can't be resolved, a distinct sandbox-specific sentinel/message is surfaced, the resolver throw is caught by the guard() wrapper (not an unhandled rejection), and the two 'no history' strings say 'the sandbox tab'. Scale: 10 = old NO_ACTIVE_TAB gone everywhere, one distinct sentinel, every resolveTabId inside the guard, both messages updated; 8 = sentinel and messages correct but one handler returns a leftover old sentinel; minScore 7.
passCriteria: Grep for the old NO_ACTIVE_TAB symbol — it must return 0 matches.
Open the goBack/goForward return paths; both must say 'the sandbox tab'.
Trace one handler's resolveTabId from call site to catch: it must be wrapped by the guard()/try-catch.
failureExamples: The dev renamed the sentinel but left one handler (often the closure) returning old NO_ACTIVE_TAB, so both coexist.
They updated the error path but forgot the two no-history message strings.
The new resolveTabId call sits outside the try/catch in one handler, so a missing sandbox throws an unhandled rejection.

rubric.label: Unit tests prove the resolved sandbox id reaches the concrete chrome API
rubric.ruleStatement: Each re-pointed handler is asserted to call resolveTabId() AND to forward the returned id (fake value 7) into the concrete chrome API, the resolver-throw path is tested, and no re-pointed-handler test retains a queryActiveTab expectation. Scale: 10 = every re-pointed handler has a forwarding assertion to id 7 plus a resolveTabId-throws→sentinel test, fakePorts retains queryActiveTab for captureTab; 8 = majority assert forwarding but the closure is indirect or throw path untested; minScore 7.
passCriteria: For each re-pointed handler, confirm an assertion that sandboxTab.resolveTabId was invoked.
For the same tests, confirm a concrete side-effect assertion that the chrome API was called with tab id 7.
Confirm a resolver-failure test exists (fake SandboxTabPorts whose resolveTabId throws → sandbox sentinel).
Confirm fakePorts still defines queryActiveTab and no re-pointed test asserts a queryActiveTab call in the resolve path.
failureExamples: The dev asserted only resolveTabId was called while a leftover queryActiveTab still feeds the chrome call — green test but production targets the active tab.
They removed the old 'no active tab' test but did not add a resolver-throw test.
They stripped queryActiveTab from fakePorts, breaking the captureTab tests and quietly deleting it.

rubric.label: SandboxTabPorts is actually wired into startServiceWorker and exercised by its test
rubric.ruleStatement: startServiceWorker constructs/passes SandboxTabPorts into pageActionHandlers, and service-worker.unit.test.ts supplies a typed fake so the wiring is exercised. Scale: 10 = startServiceWorker builds the sandbox ports once and passes them, signature matches everywhere, service-worker test passes a typed fake and goes green; 8 = prod wiring present and test green but fake is minimal; minScore 6.
passCriteria: In service-worker.ts, startServiceWorker obtains SandboxTabPorts and passes it to pageActionHandlers.
Confirm pageActionHandlers' signature declares the SandboxTabPorts parameter, so caller and signature agree.
In service-worker.unit.test.ts, startServiceWorker is invoked with a fake SandboxTabPorts and the suite runs green.
failureExamples: The dev updated the signature but startServiceWorker still calls with the old args; because the param was typed optional, tsc compiles and the feature silently no-ops in production.
Wired in prod but service-worker.unit.test.ts still constructs with old positional args, so the composition root is never exercised.

phases.healerHint: Run a grep for queryActiveTab in page-actions.ts and re-point every hit that lives outside the captureTab handler's windowId block to await sandboxTab.resolveTabId(), since the shared readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests closure is the one site that gets missed, then re-check the two no-history strings still say 'the sandbox tab'.

phases.name: Capture the sandbox tab via CDP
phases.goal: Switch the captureTab handler from the window-scoped chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab to the new CDP debugger screenshot port, so it returns a real PNG of the unfocused sandbox tab.
phases.rationale: captureTab is the one action whose current call is scoped to a window and captures whatever tab is focused — the wrong thing when the target is the backgrounded sandbox tab. The CDP port built earlier screenshots a specific tab regardless of focus, so captureTab must call it, passing the sandbox tab id.
changes: Add a CaptureDebuggerPorts parameter to pageActionHandlers, after the SandboxTabPorts parameter added in the prior phase.

Rewrite the captureTab handler to resolve the sandbox tab id and call debugger.captureScreenshot(tabId), returning { result: { dataUrl } } so the existing data:image/png result contract and the MCP server's image-block mapping stay unchanged (the CDP response is raw base64 with no dataUrl prefix; the data: prefix is added once at the CDP port layer and not re-added here).
Wire chromeCaptureDebuggerPorts() into startServiceWorker and pass it to pageActionHandlers.

Update the captureTab unit tests: assert captureScreenshot is called with the sandbox tab id (7) and the dataUrl is returned; replace the 'no active tab' captureTab test with the sandbox-resolver failure path; keep the 'chrome port rejection becomes { error }' coverage by making the debugger port reject.
inputs: the captureTab handler and its unit tests
phases.expectedResult: captureTab resolves the sandbox tab id and returns its PNG via debugger.captureScreenshot(tabId), proved by the rewritten unit tests, with the { dataUrl: 'data:image/png;base64,...' } result contract and the MCP image block unchanged. The horizon then requires a live-Chrome check (drive the sandbox tab while a DIFFERENT tab is focused and confirm the PNG shows the sandbox tab) before it can close as MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING.
phases.compensation: If a later phase forces reverting CDP capture, captureTab can be restored to captureVisibleTab — but that restores the focused-tab-only limitation, so this is the point of the change. Revert by restoring the old captureTab body and removing the CaptureDebuggerPorts parameter.

rubric.label: Data-URL PNG result contract
rubric.ruleStatement: captureTab returns { result: { dataUrl } } where dataUrl is a fully-qualified data:image/png;base64,<b64> URI, byte-equivalent in shape to the pre-change contract so the MCP image-block mapping stays untouched. Scale: 10 = complete validly-prefixed PNG data-URI with prefix re-emitted exactly once; 8 = correct re-emit backed by a test asserting the full prefixed string; minScore 6.
passCriteria: Read the captureTab handler's success return: it returns { result: { dataUrl } } where dataUrl starts with the literal 'data:image/png;base64,'.
Confirm the base64 body is the CDP response's raw base64 passed straight through — no decode-then-re-encode, no added/removed chars.
Confirm the prefix appears exactly once — no doubled prefix.
A test asserts the returned dataUrl equals 'data:image/png;base64,' + the mocked base64 fixture.
Search the diff for the MCP-side block that renders result.dataUrl and confirm it still reads the same string.
failureExamples: The dev returns the raw CDP base64 with no data: prefix, so a test asserting 'dataUrl is a string' passes but the MCP block renders nothing.
The success path returns { result: { base64 } } instead of { result: { dataUrl } }, so the MCP mapping can't find result.dataUrl.
The prefix uses the wrong mime type or the PNG is re-encoded, producing a mangled image.

rubric.label: Sandbox tab routed through the CDP port, not the focused tab
rubric.ruleStatement: captureTab resolves the sandbox tab's tabId and calls debugger.captureScreenshot(tabId); the sandbox path has no fallback to window-scoped captureVisibleTab. Scale: 10 = captureScreenshot invoked with the exact resolved sandbox tabId, no captureVisibleTab branch in the sandbox path, test asserts the correct id and that the focused/id-window id is NOT passed; 8 = correct call made and asserted; minScore 7.
passCriteria: The captureTab handler resolves the sandbox tab's tabId from the resolver and passes it as the first argument to debugger.captureScreenshot().
Confirm captureTab calls the same resolver used by the prior phase, not re-deriving the id from the active tab/document.activeElement.
Search page-actions.ts for captureVisibleTab — the only remaining call sits outside the sandbox-tab path.
The captureTab test asserts captureScreenshot is called with 7 and NOT with the focused/active tab id.
Confirm a tabId is passed, not a windowId.
failureExamples: The handler calls captureScreenshot(resolvedId) but resolvedId is the sandbox WINDOW id, so CDP targets the wrong entity.
The handler still calls captureVisibleTab for the sandbox path 'just in case', so with the sandbox backgrounded it returns the focused tab's PNG.
captureScreenshot is called but the awaited base64 is dropped, so dataUrl resolves to 'data:image/png;base64,undefined'.

rubric.label: Failure-path result contract
rubric.ruleStatement: When the sandbox resolver fails or the CDP debugger port rejects, captureTab returns { error: <readable message> } — the same shape the previous captureTab produced on failure — not a throw, log-and-undefined, or partial success. Scale: 10 = both the resolver-failure and debugger-rejection paths return { error }, both covered by tests, old 'no active tab' test gone; 8 = port-rejection→{error} preserved and resolver-failure test added; minScore 6.
passCriteria: When resolving the sandbox tab fails the handler returns { error: '...' } — no throw and no partial { result: ... }.
When debugger.captureScreenshot rejects, the handler catches it and returns { error: <message> }; it does not re-throw.
A test drives the debugger port to reject and asserts { error } without throwing; a separate test drives the resolver to fail and asserts the same shape.
Confirm the error value is a readable string naming the cause, not an Error object or a generic message.
failureExamples: The dev keeps the old 'no active tab' test repointed at the resolver but leaves the port-rejection path to throw, so a test with a rejecting port fails and the MCP tool never resolves.
The catch converts a CDP rejection into { result: { dataUrl: undefined } } or returns undefined.
Every failure path returns the identical 'Could not capture tab' message, making errors indistinguishable.

rubric.label: Live wiring of the debugger ports at startup
rubric.ruleStatement: CaptureDebuggerPorts is genuinely constructed at service-worker startup and passed into pageActionHandlers in the correct position (immediately after SandboxTabPorts), so the CDP port is real at runtime. Scale: 10 = startServiceWorker builds and threads it in the documented position, the handler reads captureScreenshot off that position, typecheck confirms it is passed; 8 = constructed and passed; minScore 6.
passCriteria: In service-worker.ts, startServiceWorker calls chromeCaptureDebuggerPorts() and passes the result into pageActionHandlers alongside SandboxTabPorts.
In page-actions.ts, the signature declares a CaptureDebuggerPorts parameter immediately after SandboxTabPorts, and captureTab reads captureScreenshot from that position.
Confirm the argument at the call site and the parameter order match.
Run the chrome-bridge typecheck (tsc --noEmit) and confirm clean.
failureExamples: The dev updates pageActionHandlers and all unit tests pass (each builds its own mock), but startServiceWorker never builds/passes the real debugger ports — runtime captureTab's debugger object is undefined and throws.
The debugger ports are passed in the wrong position, so captureTab reads the sandbox-ports object as the debugger port.
The parameter is typed optional so typecheck passes even though nothing wires it, and the handler silently falls back to captureVisibleTab.

phases.healerHint: CDP's Page.captureScreenshot returns bare base64 with no data: prefix, so the most likely miss is a green test that passes the raw base64 through while the MCP image block then renders nothing — re-emit the 'data:image/png;base64,' prefix in the captureTab success return and assert the full prefixed string in the unit test.

successCriteria: The extension lazily creates ONE dedicated sandbox tab on first need, reuses the same tab across subsequent commands; its tabId is persisted in chrome.storage.local so it survives a service-worker suspension, and a missing/stale tabId is validated and transparently recreated before the next act.

verify-background-tab-debugger-attach: A recorded real-Chrome verdict that chrome.debugger can attach to a background tab from the service worker and Page.captureScreenshot returns that background tab's PNG, with the 'debugger' permission added to the manifest.
add-sandbox-tab-port: A new sandbox-ports.ts exporting the SandboxTabPorts interface and chromeSandboxTabPorts() implementation, covered by sandbox-ports.unit.test.ts for every exported symbol.

add-cdp-screenshot-port: A new debugger-ports.ts exporting the CaptureDebuggerPorts interface and chromeCaptureDebuggerPorts() implementation, covered by debugger-ports.unit.test.ts, with the CDP-vs-DOM decision recorded as limited to Page.captureScreenshot.

Every existing page action (getPageText, readPage, findElement, clickElement, typeText, executeScript, clickAt, hover, navigateTo/Back/Forward, reloadTab, readConsoleMessages, readNetworkRequests) now resolves its target to the sandbox tab's tabId instead of queryActiveTab().

The CDP-vs-DOM fork decision is made and recorded explicitly: option (a) — CDP ONLY for the captureTab background-tab gap — chosen; option (b) — broader CDP pivot — explicitly NOT chosen and deferred.

tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, and the package's vitest suite all pass; the manifest gains the 'debugger' permission without breaking the existing suite; boky's extension/bridge/verify pipeline is unchanged.

The horizon closes only after the live Chrome check runs (per the project rule that a horizon changing the extension ends 'blocked / MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING'), proving the sandbox tab is drivable and screenshottable while unfocused.
deferred: Broad CDP pivot beyond the screenshot gap (Runtime.evaluate to replace executeScript, Input.dispatchKeyEvent / trusted drag, page scrolling, full-page scroll-capture, file upload) — option (a) keeps the stack DOM except Page.captureScreenshot; option (b) is explicitly deferred (YAGNI 1: not asked for this horizon).

The result-size-cap location/threshold decision (extension-side per-action vs generic MCP-layer vs none) — still OPEN and deliberately deferred (YAGNI 3: no decision to implement yet).

Preserving the active-tab path as a selectable per-call option — the sandbox tab replaces the default target; retained 'active tab' alternative deferred under the user's 'human never picks or switches' decision (YAGNI 1: not asked for).

Remove the now-unused queryActiveTab, captureVisibleTab, and ActiveTab.windowId from ChromePorts — the active-tab path becomes dead; the package has no dead-code gate so leaving it is harmless, removal is interface churn for a later cleanup horizon (YAGNI 1-2: not asked for, not blocking).
Auto-navigation of the sandbox tab to a fixed bootstrap URL on creation — the agent drives navigation via the existing navigateTo action (YAGNI 3: speculative).
Boky's extension / BridgeRelayModule / extension-mcp.mjs — unchanged everywhere; chrome-bridge is standalone and boky is never migrated into it.
